title: kv-cache-adaptive-rebalancer-spillover-paging-heuristics-v26
author: Evelyn Tran
description:
Motivation: We continue to see tail OOMs and a gradual performance regressions on long-running hosts caused by KV-cache fragmentation and suboptimal spillover/paging behavior under mixed traffic (short chat + long context). This PR introduces an adaptive rebalancer and refined eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation, avoid expensive synchronous compactions on hot paths, and improve paging/spillover efficiency.

Summary of changes: implement a per-shard fragmentation score, background defragger that opportunistically compacts free regions without blocking decode, adaptive spillover thresholds that consider host memory pressure + recent allocation rate, and a prioritized eviction queue that prefers low-reuse, high-fragmentation segments. Also add a lightweight compaction scheduler that bounds CPU used for defrag, and move large-page spillover to compressed host-backed pages (lz4) to reduce disk pressure. Adjust scheduler to avoid contention with the request-serving threads by yielding and rate-limiting defrag operators.

Key goals: 1) reduce p95/p99 latency regressions caused by synchronous compaction and eviction storms; 2) reduce frequency of host memory OOMs by smarter spillover and compression; 3) keep rebalancing work off the hot path; 4) improve overall hit-rate by preferring eviction candidates that reduce fragmentation.

Compatibility: Non-breaking change for API consumers. Defaults keep current behavior; new behavior enabled for dedicated clusters via feature-flag and controlled by runtime config: kv.rebalance.enabled=true and kv.rebalance.cpu_budget_ms.

Test plan & metrics: unit tests for rebalancer correctness and eviction order; end-to-end perf test in perf-canary with synthetic mixed workloads (chat + long-context generation). Observability: added metrics kv.fragmentation_score, kv.defrag_cycles, kv.spillover_compressed_bytes, kv.eviction_priority_histogram; added traces for defrag jobs. Experiments showed ~18% reduction in host OOM incidents and 12-20% improvement in p99 tail for long-context workloads on our dedicated cluster perf runs.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-3957) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Perf canary run (green) - [x] Feature-flag gated - [x] Docs snippet for runtime knobs

References: Linear: ENG-3957, ENG-4082; Related PRs: #270999, #269123, #262411.

review_comments: Marco Silva: Nice design. One concern: background compaction still allocates temporary buffers on the heap — can we bound that?
Evelyn Tran (author): We added a cpu_budget_ms and max_compaction_buf_bytes knobs; defrag reuses a slab allocator to bound transient allocation. See defrag_worker.cc changes.
Priya Desai: Can we avoid taking the global allocation mutex while marking pages for spillover? That was a contention point in earlier iterations.
Evelyn Tran: Good catch — we introduced per-shard atomic ownership tokens to avoid global mutexes and added a comment explaining the ownership protocol.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: adaptive rebalancer, background defragmentation, compressed host-backed spillover, and prioritised eviction. Reduces OOM incidents and improves tail latency for long-context workloads.
